text: Vaccines train the immune system to recognize pathogens and help prevent infection or severe disease.
source: World Health Organization

text: Sudden one-sided weakness, confusion, speech trouble, vision trouble, balance trouble, or a severe headache can signal stroke and needs emergency care.
source: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

text: Antibiotics do not treat viruses; unnecessary use can cause side effects and antimicrobial resistance.
source: U.S. Food and Drug Administration

text: Suspected heart attack requires an immediate call to emergency services; delaying care can cause serious harm.
source: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute

text: Insulin helps glucose move from blood into cells for energy and helps store glucose for later use.
source: National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases

text: People should read medicine labels, follow warnings, check active ingredients, and ask a pharmacist when unsure.
source: World Health Organization

text: Soap and water or alcohol-based sanitizer helps remove germs; hands should be cleaned at important times.
source: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

text: High blood pressure often has no symptoms, so measurement is important; uncontrolled pressure raises cardiovascular risk.
source: U.S. Food and Drug Administration

text: Healthy eating, physical activity, and healthy weight can help prevent or delay type 2 diabetes.
source: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute

text: Adequate sleep supports physical health, emotional well-being, attention, and memory.
source: National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases

text: Regular activity can improve heart health, strengthen bones and muscles, support mental health, and reduce chronic disease risk.
source: World Health Organization

text: Dehydration occurs when fluid loss exceeds intake; thirst, dry mouth, dark urine, dizziness, or confusion can occur.
source: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

text: Food allergy symptoms can include hives, swelling, vomiting, wheezing, or breathing difficulty; severe reactions need emergency care.
source: U.S. Food and Drug Administration

text: Asthma can cause wheezing, breathlessness, chest tightness, and coughing; action plans and prescribed treatments help manage it.
source: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute

text: Tuberculosis is a bacterial disease commonly affecting the lungs and spreads through air from active pulmonary disease.
source: National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases

text: Malaria is caused by parasites transmitted by infected mosquitoes; suspected malaria needs prompt evaluation.
source: World Health Organization

text: Mental health supports coping and relationships; mental health conditions are common and treatable.
source: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

text: Depression can involve persistent low mood or loss of interest and changes in sleep, appetite, energy, or concentration.
source: U.S. Food and Drug Administration

text: Ultraviolet radiation causes skin cancer; shade, protective clothing, and sunscreen reduce exposure.
source: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute

text: Quitting smoking lowers cancer, heart disease, stroke, and respiratory disease risk; counseling and medicines can help.
source: National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases

text: Alcohol-related health risks vary by amount and pattern; drinking less generally reduces risk.
source: World Health Organization

text: High LDL cholesterol can contribute to artery plaque and cardiovascular risk; testing and clinician assessment guide care.
source: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

text: Early chronic kidney disease may have no symptoms; blood and urine tests can detect kidney damage or reduced function.
source: U.S. Food and Drug Administration

text: Some vaccines are recommended during pregnancy while others may be delayed; decisions should follow current clinical guidance.
source: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute

text: Antimicrobial resistance occurs when germs no longer respond to medicines; appropriate use helps slow resistance.
source: National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases

text: Concussion is a traumatic brain injury; worsening symptoms or danger signs require urgent medical evaluation.
source: World Health Organization

text: Cool running water may help a minor thermal burn; ice, butter, or grease should not be applied to burns.
source: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

text: Suspected poisoning requires immediate emergency or poison-center advice; do not induce vomiting unless instructed.
source: U.S. Food and Drug Administration

text: People should follow prescribing instructions and discuss changes to prescribed medicines with a healthcare professional.
source: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute

text: A symptom alone does not establish a diagnosis; assessment may require history, examination, and appropriate tests.
source: National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases
